name: 46,XY Difference of Sex Development Due to a Testosterone Synthesis Defect
aliases: 46,XY DSD due to Testosterone Biosynthesis Deficiency
46,XY Disorder of Sex Development with Impaired Testosterone Production

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Biochemical Diagnostic Criteria for 46,XY DSD due to Testosterone Synthesis Defect

criteria.description: Identification of pathogenic variants in genes involved in testosterone biosynthesis (e.g., HSD17B3, SRD5A2, CYP17A1)
Low serum testosterone levels with elevated precursors or altered testosterone to dihydrotestosterone ratio
Presence of undervirilized external genitalia in a 46,XY individual (e.g., micropenis, hypospadias, ambiguous genitalia)
Imaging evidence of testes in typical or ectopic locations
Abnormal response to human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) stimulation test indicating impaired testosterone synthesis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of undervirilized genitalia in a 46,XY individual plus biochemical evidence of impaired testosterone synthesis and/or pathogenic genetic variants in testosterone biosynthesis genes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, biochemical, and genetic data; differential diagnosis includes androgen insensitivity syndromes and other forms of 46,XY DSD.

pathognomonic.notes: Includes micropenis, hypospadias, and bifid scrotum

common.symptomName: Delayed or absent virilization at puberty
searchTerms: late or no male puberty changes
breast tissue growth in teenage boys
short distance between anus and genitals

occasional.symptomName: Mild hypospadias with normal penile length
Psychosocial distress related to ambiguous genitalia
searchTerms: mental health issues due to genital ambiguity

occasional.symptomName: Mild gynecomastia without other endocrine abnormalities
searchTerms: slight male breast growth without hormone issues

rare.notes: In cases with CYP17A1 mutations affecting adrenal steroidogenesis
searchTerms: high blood pressure from adrenal gland problems

rare.notes: Rare in isolated testosterone synthesis defects

laboratory: Low serum testosterone with elevated precursors (e.g., androstenedione)
Elevated LH and FSH levels indicating gonadotropin feedback
imaging: Ultrasound or MRI showing presence and location of testes
Absence of Müllerian structures on pelvic imaging
genetic: Pathogenic variants in HSD17B3, SRD5A2, CYP17A1, or other testosterone biosynthesis genes
other: Abnormal response to hCG stimulation test
Histopathology of gonadal tissue showing normal testicular architecture

distinguishingFeatures: Normal or elevated testosterone levels with androgen receptor mutations
Absent or sparse pubic and axillary hair
Normal testosterone levels with impaired conversion to dihydrotestosterone
Virialization at puberty despite undervirilized genitalia at birth

redFlags: Ambiguous genitalia in a newborn with 46,XY karyotype
Failure to virilize at puberty in a genetically male individual
Severe hypospadias or micropenis requiring surgical intervention
references: Hughes IA, et al. Consensus statement on management of intersex disorders. Arch Dis Child. 2006.
Maimoun L, et al. 46,XY disorders of sex development: clinical and genetic aspects. Ann Endocrinol (Paris). 2011.
Orphanet Report Series: 46,XY difference of sex development due to testosterone synthesis defect. Orphanet. 2023.
